html:
The Somers Isles Company was the English joint-stock company that owned and ran Bermuda from 1615 to 1684. Its name came from Admiral George Somers of the Sea Venture.

The company divided the islands into shares and tribes, still the names of Bermuda's parishes. It pushed tobacco growing and set up an assembly in 1620, one of the oldest in the English colonies.

Enslaved Africans and Native Americans were brought in from early on. Planters complained that the company stifled trade, and the crown took over in 1684. Bermudians then turned to the sea, building ships and raking salt in the Turks Islands, within the English Atlantic.
sum: The Somers Isles Company was the English joint-stock company that owned and ran Bermuda from 1615 to 1684. Its name came from Admiral George Somers of the Sea Venture.
